__comment__: WHY POSITION Y IS LARGE AND NOT 0
The geometry's root bone is bound to the hand with
which is what attaches it to the player at all. Bedrock then applies a
-1.5 metre (-24 unit) offset to a bound attachable, so a model authored
around the origin lands down at the player's feet. The +24 cancels it out.
The remainder centres the model. The geometry runs y=-2.0..+13.5, so
its centre sits at y=+5.75; that centre, scaled, is subtracted so the
MIDDLE of the model lands on the hand instead of its base.
sitting at the feet again ... position[1] lost its +24
floating above the hand ..... lower position[1]
hanging below the hand ...... raise position[1]
size wrong .................. change scale, then redo the sum above
Left square-on rather than three-quarter: the tool is not a flat object,
so it already reads as solid from any angle.
